features.name: Phenotype: extract embedded HPO terms
features.description: The challenge supplies phenotype 'as standardized HPO terms' and the docx already carries 8 embedded HP:####### IDs. Write scripts/extract_hpo.py to pull the HP: IDs from word/document.xml with stdlib zipfile, fetch and provenance-record hp.obo, resolve labels, and write notes/phenotype.md. Reduce the Presentation and Notes cells to broad, non-verbatim lexical signals without emitting clinical narrative, exact ages, dates, or measurements. The broader toolchain and annotation-resource bundle remains feat-003. Also record the negative: the document names no karyotype, no prior genetic testing, no candidate gene - so the search must stay genome-wide rather than collapsing onto BUB1B/CEP57/TRIP13.
features.evidence: scripts/extract_hpo.py; `uv run python scripts/extract_hpo.py --self-check` proves HPO extraction, OBO lookup, Presentation/Notes classification, and that source text is not emitted; `uv run python scripts/extract_hpo.py` wrote notes/phenotype.md with 8 HPO ID/label rows and fixed-vocabulary context signals. Exact wording, ages, dates, numbers, and measurements remain local. hp.obo release 2026-06-23, SHA-256 a5092cbdf605f568403cf7380d9173014015692433b2cc631bc5c1b053876b1b. features.name: Toolchain and annotation resources
features.description: Nothing is installed on this box - no bcftools, samtools, tabix, bwa-mem2, vep, gatk, nextflow, pigz. AGENTS.md referenced scripts/get_tools.sh and tools/; this feature creates them. Also fetch the reference resources: the GRCh38 no-alt analysis set FASTA matching the VCF header, VEP cache (GRCh38), gnomAD v4 allele frequencies, ClinVar, and hp.obo. Outbound network to Ensembl / gnomAD GCS / UCSC / OBO / GitHub is confirmed reachable. Budget disk against the 3.3 TB free on /mnt/md0 and record every version in tools/.

features.name: VCF triage baseline
features.description: Annotate the provided joint VCF and produce the first candidate table - the reproducible baseline every later ranking is compared against. Known specifics: keep PASS only (4,740,790 of 5,012,204), drop the 116,485 records on alt/random/decoy contigs, and carry the no-chr <-> chr conversion explicitly since submissions are matched by exact tuple equality. Primary genetic model is COMPOUND HETEROZYGOUS (two rare damaging alleles in one gene) - both the scoring code's answer key and the absence of any ROH point there; de novo dominant is the second model. Rank with the feat-002 HPO terms (Exomiser / LIRICAL style).

features.name: GC-corrected copy-number and BAF screen
features.description: The provided VCF contains no CNV or structural records at all (genotypes are only 0/1, 1/1, 1/2), so MVA's defining mosaic aneuploidy is invisible in it. A quick 10 Mb BAF/depth screen (notes/data-profile.md) excluded high-level aneuploidy but left chr20 (and 19, 22) unresolved and confounded with GC/mappability bias. Redo it properly with GC-corrected read-depth binning and a mappability mask so the chr20 signal is either confirmed as low-level mosaic trisomy or attributed to bias. Small and targeted - this does not require re-calling the genome.

features.name: Targeted realignment for missed alleles
features.description: OPTIONAL, contingent on feat-004's candidate list. Justification is recovering a second compound-het allele that Sentieon's diploid germline caller could have dropped - deep-intronic, structural, or repeat-adjacent - NOT aneuploidy detection, which feat-005a handles more cheaply. Realign the 8 FASTQ lanes (or only the intervals around surviving candidates) and re-call with a mosaic-aware caller. Real cost: ~385 GB decompressed, zcat alone is ~1 h serial, and the box is contended (load avg 109 on 64 cores, 3 of 5 A100s busy). nohup into logs/ and never block the session.

features.name: Local scorer and submission conformance
features.description: Only 6 Track 1 submissions exist; none should be spent discovering a formatting bug. Vendor the challenge's public evaluation.py and track1_submission_template.csv into scripts/ and self-score every candidate CSV locally first. Must enforce: proband_id is exactly PROBAND01; chrom fields are chr-prefixed (the scorer only .strip()s them, so unprefixed names silently score zero); at most 10 rows; strictly distinct epcr values in (0,1] since ties collapse F-max thresholds; indels left-aligned and represented as the answer key would have them. Strategy note: rows with epcr BELOW the true row are free - they cannot lower F-max and do not move rank points - so fill all 10.

features.name: Make this repository public
features.description: Every Track 1 submission requires a GitHub URL starting with https://github.com/ - this blocks the submission, it is not a Track 2 afterthought. History is currently clean (4 commits, 15 tracked files, nothing ever under data/ results/ logs/). Re-audit history at the time with 'git log --all --pretty=format: --name-only', confirm .gitignore and the pre-commit gate still hold, flip visibility on origin, and record the URL here.

features.name: Track 1 submission
features.description: Ranked variant CSV matching static/templates/track1_submission_template.csv (proband_id, chrom/pos/ref/alt per allele, epcr, finding_type, notes), self-scored via feat-006. Three hard requirements at upload: the CSV, a report file (.pdf or .md) describing the approach, and the public GitHub URL from feat-007. Scored on rank points (rank 1 = 100, ranks 2-3 = 50, 4-5 = 25, 6-10 = 10, partial match 0.5x) and F-max. Limit 6 submissions; best one counts.

features.name: Track 2 drug repurposing report
features.description: Mechanism characterization for the top variant(s) and approved-drug candidates targeting the disrupted pathway. Deliverables: detailed report, public GitHub link, and a 3-minute recorded pitch video. Judged on rigor 35 / impact 25 / innovation 25 / scalability 15. Limit 1 submission, no re-submissions. The organizers state publicly that care for this child 'means managing symptoms and fighting cancer cells' - cancer predisposition is part of the phenotype and should anchor the mechanism argument (BUB1B/MVA1 is the canonical link).
